name: Bright Particular Star
description: A romantic neural-feed drama in which you inhabit Ines Volkov-Adeyemi, a Tier 3 logistics analyst who falls into a dangerous affair with a Spire heir while uncovering evidence of her company's involvement in food-supply manipulation — the film's central innovation being that romantic and moral tension are neurologically indistinguishable, forcing you to feel desire and dread as the same sensation. Vantablack's highest-grossing non-action release of the decade, it was distributed in 22 languages simultaneously and remains in the top-100 all-time neural-feed viewings.
cultural_impact: The film's signature neural technique — called 'bright particular' by fans — became a benchmark and a byword: 'that's very bright particular' means something is deliberately designed to make you want what's hurting you.
story_hooks: The food-supply manipulation subplot was based on real corporate intelligence that a Vantablack script researcher uncovered and wove into the fiction — the researcher was later transferred to a position with no external communication.

Someone has modified a bootleg copy of Bright Particular to replace the Spire heir character with a specific, real Spire resident — and is selling the experience as a personalized fantasy to that resident's enemies.

The actress who provided the base neural-template for Ines Volkov-Adeyemi claims she never consented to the emotional architecture being derived from her actual neurological responses during the recording sessions.
